newsitem.title: DUBAI: ARAB STATES URGED TO STREAMLINE ACCOUNTING RULES.
newsitem.headline: ARAB STATES URGED TO STREAMLINE ACCOUNTING RULES.

text.p: The International Accounting Standards Committee (IASC) and the Arab Society of Certified Accountants (ACSA) on Thursday called on all Arab countries to adopt streamlined accounting standards by 1998.

"We have jointly concluded that it would be in the best interests of the Arab world if all Arab countries commit to the adoption of International Accounting Standards (IAS) for financial reporting purposes no later than 1998," IASC Chairman Michael Sharpe and ASCA President Talal Abu-Ghazaleh said.
In a joint statement issued after the Global Accounting Standards forum in Dubai, they said the adoption of IAS would "greatly help the economic development and capital flow into the region".
Investors in Arab states regularly cite poor and differing methods of financial reporting by Arab firms as an obstacle to investment.
In many Arab countries, most of which are trying to lure foreign cash and give the private sector a bigger role, disclosure levels are low and there is limited financial transparency.
For over 20 years, the IASC has been working to create and implement a set of accounting standards which are the same throughout the world.

"Providing information in accordance with a known set of accounting standards which are high quality, transparent and comparable reduces investment risk and lowers the cost of capital," Sharpe said in a separate statement.
